metadata.title: An Architectural Approach to Regenerative Software
metadata.subtitle: Keep the system. Delete the code.
metadata.speaker: Chad Fowler

slides.title: What If Your Software Rebuilt Itself?
slides.subtitle: If changing software is hard, do it all the time.
on_slide_text: If I deleted your implementation tomorrow, what would have to survive for the system to remain itself?

slides.title: The Long Version
slides.subtitle: Regenerative Software. Final in April 2027.

slides.title: Ask Anything.
slides.subtitle: No Q&A slot. This board is where your questions go.

slides.title: The Plan.
slides.kicker: All of this, around the clock, seriously

lines.text: No code review. Nobody reads the code.
Nobody writes a prompt. Production does.
It never stops. Day and night, whatever passes CI ships.
Humans don't pick the language or the stack anymore.
The spec comes later.
Delete the source to find out what you don't know.
Throw away the history. Keep the decisions.

slides.title: This Is What We'd Been Training For.
slides.subtitle: Heartbleed. Every service rebuilt in a day. Zero application code changed.

slides.title: Small Is Not Replaceable.
slides.subtitle: What made it unreplaceable was not inside it.

slides.title: Relocating Rigor
slides.kicker: Every one of these looked reckless
slides.subtitle: When the economics change, the rigor moves. Look for where. If you can't find it, worry.

lines.text: XP. Plans became working code, delivered frequently and consistently.
Ruby & Rails. Static type checks became tests and fast feedback.
Continuous deployment. Release windows became rollback and observability.
Regeneration. Hand-written code becomes what?

slides.title: If the Code Can Burn, What Cannot?
slides.subtitle: Same promises, kept. Same reasons, recorded.

lines.label: Intent
lines.text: What must stay true. Not how the code works.

lines.label: Architecture
lines.text: The target the code compiles into. What no implementation may do.

lines.label: Evaluations
lines.text: How we know a replacement is right.

lines.label: Provenance
lines.text: Why every decision was made, and what it ruled out.

slides.title: rm -rf src
slides.subtitle: If your stomach drops, that's not recklessness. It's not knowing what would survive.
on_slide_text: NODE TODAY. RUST TOMORROW. SAME CONTRACT.

slides.title: The Regeneration Test
slides.kicker: A test for what counts as architecture
slides.quote: If I regenerated the system tomorrow and this changed, would I care?

slides.title: Code Is a Compiled Artifact.
slides.subtitle: Intent → Architecture → Code

slides.title: The Loop
slides.subtitle: People approve intent and policy. The gate judges code. Risk decides who else signs.

slides.title: The Spec Is Not a Document.
slides.subtitle: A connected body of knowledge with consequences. You query it; you never read it top to bottom.

slides.title: From Conversation to Code, and Back
slides.subtitle: Every artifact on this slide is real.

slides.title: Every Line Traces Back to a Clause.
slides.kicker: Phoenix inspector · the library example, live
slides.subtitle: Pick a constraint: the clause it came from, the unit that owns it, the file it compiled to. Pick a file: the same path, backwards.

slides.title: Evaluations Survive Rewrites.
slides.subtitle: If a different language would invalidate it, it's at the wrong boundary.

slides.title: Isn't This Just Code Generation?
slides.kicker: Live · the board you have been using
slides.subtitle: Your questions have to survive all three.

lines.label: Intent
lines.text: One spec line changes. One unit of four regenerates. Your questions survive.

lines.label: Evidence
lines.text: Why every line exists, and what the gate would refuse.

lines.label: Runtime
lines.text: Same spec, same evaluations. The server becomes Python.

slides.title: The Implementation Remembers.
slides.quote: What does this implementation know that we have forgotten?

slides.title: Production Writes the Prompt.
slides.kicker: One lap, overnight · nothing changed but the world
slides.subtitle: The spec never changed. The world did. Nobody had to wake up.

lines.label: Spec
lines.text: “Order history loads in under 200 ms.” Nobody touches it again.

lines.label: Launch
lines.text: 3,000 orders, sorted in memory. 40 ms. The gate passes.

lines.label: Drift
lines.text: Eighteen months later: 4 million orders, 900 ms. No code changed. No spec changed.

lines.label: Observe
lines.text: 2 a.m.: the latency claim fails in production. The intent still holds, so no one is paged.

lines.label: Regenerate
lines.text: Only the history unit, now told what production knows: an indexed, paged query.

lines.label: Verify
lines.text: Same evaluation, at production size: 60 ms. Swapped in before anyone wakes.

slides.title: Not Everything Regenerates at the Same Speed.
slides.kicker: Pace, and the state nobody wrote down
slides.subtitle: Fast layers churn on top of slow contracts. And the state is never where you think.

slides.title: Delete Safely. Then Compact.
slides.subtitle: Every step is a question about state. Only one touches code. Regeneration without compaction is faster accumulation.

lines.label: Compat
lines.text: The old path keeps emitting what it emitted, through the new code.

lines.label: Migrate
lines.text: Move known consumers one at a time.

lines.label: Isolate
lines.text: The old path complains loudly on every use. Hidden dependencies announce themselves.

lines.label: Remove
lines.text: Only after nothing has tripped the alarm for long enough.

lines.label: Observe
lines.text: Keep watching. Long enough is a judgment.

lines.label: Compact
lines.text: Fold what you learned into the spec.

slides.title: The Spec Can Come Later.
slides.subtitle: The first implementation is how you discover what you mean. For the first time, you can afford to throw it away.

slides.title: How a System Becomes Regenerative
slides.kicker: One unit at a time, one rung at a time

lines.label: Replaceable
lines.text: A real boundary and evaluations. Delete the unit, get it back.

lines.label: Remembered
lines.text: Decisions and rejections captured as you work, not reconstructed.

lines.label: Gated
lines.text: Evaluations and constraints are the review. Where risk allows, you stop reading the diff.

lines.label: Selective
lines.text: A spec change regenerates only what it touches. You stop editing code.

lines.label: Closed
lines.text: Production evidence becomes failed claims. You stop writing prompts.

slides.title: Start With the Boring Component.
slides.subtitle: Strongest evaluations. Smallest blast radius.
